description: padStart zero-pads identifiers to a fixed width, and an identifier that already holds the width keeps all of it
padEnd aligns labels in a column, padding with one space when no fill is given
A clock reading pads its hours and minutes to two digits each
A fill of several characters is repeated and cut to the missing count, keeping its start
An empty fill, or text that already holds the length, gives the text unchanged
A padded declaration follows later writes of its receiver, its length and its fill
code:
label = "7"
width = 3
fill = "0"
shown = label.padStart(width, fill)
label = "42"
width = 5
fill = "*"
shown

description: A class-level rule pads the number of each instance on its own
code:
class Ticket(id):
    this.id = id
$Ticket.code = "T-" + String($Ticket.id).padStart(4, "0")
first = Ticket(7)
second = Ticket(42)
first.id = 123
[first.code, second.code]

description: The length converts as the count of repeat does: fractions truncate, numeric strings and true convert, and negatives or NaN pad nothing
The keyword undefined is null and fills with its text, while a missing property fills with spaces
Lengths count characters, so text and fills outside ASCII pad one character at a time
A result too large to allocate raises a TypeError, and the failed write is rolled back
code:
width = 3
shown = "7".padStart(width, "0")
failure = ""
try:
    width = 1 / 0
catch error:
    failure = error
[failure, width, shown]

description: Padding stays a string method: a null receiver gives undefined and a number keeps its TypeError
code:
n = null
result = ""
try:
    result = (5).padStart(3, "0")
catch error:
    result = error
[n.padStart(3), result]

description: A report line pads its label with dots and its price with spaces, and follows both
code:
item = "tea"
price = "4"
line = item.padEnd(8, ".") + price.padStart(3)
item = "honey"
price = "12"
line
